commit.message: external/webserver: fix gpt cyber issue of webserver

apps/examples/: Add crashrpt_test application for crash diagnostic capture

Add crashrpt_test example application that demonstrates the /dev/crashrpt
driver functionality. The application allocates diagnostic data structures
(500 nodes of 48 bytes, 50 nodes of 64 bytes) and registers a reporter
thread that serializes all data to a file when the system asserts.

The reporter runs at high priority and uses atomic file operations
(write to temp file + rename) to ensure reports are never partially written.

Add crashrpt_comprehensive_test for crash report validation

Update the crashrpt comprehensive test to retain only APP_ASSERT and
KERNEL_ASSERT test cases for focused crash reporting validation.

+CRASH REPORT COMPREHENSIVE TEST
+================================
+
+Demonstration and test application for the /dev/crashrpt crash diagnostic
+capture driver. This application tests selected crash scenarios that can
+be triggered from user-space and verifies the generated crash reports.
+
+
+WHAT IT DOES
+------------
+
+The application provides test cases for different crash types:
+
+  TC1: APP_ASSERT     - Direct ASSERT(0) from application
+                        Expected reason code: 2
+
+  TC2: KERNEL_ASSERT  - Kernel assert via /dev/null ioctl
+                        Expected reason code: 3
+                        Note: Triggers ASSERT() in dev_null driver
+
+
+SEQUENCE
+--------
+
+  1. The application creates a reporter thread that registers through
+     /dev/crashrpt and parks in fin_wait().
+
+  2. A test command is issued (e.g., "crashrpt_comprehensive_test app_assert").
+
+  3. The test triggers a crash. At the very start of up_assert(), before
+     any crash handling begins, the kernel wakes the reporter and waits.
+
+  4. The reporter writes a text report containing test metadata and tells
+     the driver it is finished.
+
+  5. Assert handling continues and the board reboots.
+
+  6. After reboot, use "verify" or "verify_all" commands to validate reports.
+
+
+WHY TEXT REPORTS
+----------------
+
+Unlike the basic crashrpt_test which writes binary diagnostic data, this
+application writes human-readable text reports for easier verification:
+
+  CRASH REPORT
+  Test Case: 1
+  Expected Reason: 2
+  Actual Reason: 2
+  Report Sequence: 0
+
+This makes it simple to verify that:
+  - The crash was captured
+  - The reason code matches expectations
+  - The reporter executed correctly
+
+
+USAGE
+-----
+
+From TASH shell:
+
+  # Initialize and run test (combined command)
+  crashrpt_comprehensive_test app_assert
+  crashrpt_comprehensive_test kernel_assert
+
+  # Check status
+  crashrpt_comprehensive_test status
+
+  # Verify reports after reboot
+  crashrpt_comprehensive_test verify                    # Verify last report
+  crashrpt_comprehensive_test verify /tmp/crashrpt_r0.bin  # Specific file
+  crashrpt_comprehensive_test verify_all                # All reports
+
+
+EXAMPLE SESSION
+---------------
+
+  TASH>> crashrpt_comprehensive_test app_assert
+  crashrpt_ct: TC1 - Testing APP_ASSERT
+  crashrpt_ct: About to call ASSERT(0)...
+  crashrpt_ct: reporter registered and waiting (TC1)
+  crashrpt_ct: woken, reason 2 (expected: 2)
+  crashrpt_ct: report written to /tmp/crashrpt_r0.bin
+  ... assert output follows, then the board reboots ...
+
+  [After reboot]
+
+  TASH>> crashrpt_comprehensive_test verify_all
+  crashrpt_ct: Scanning for reports in /tmp
+
+  ===========================================
+  Verifying: /tmp/crashrpt_r0.bin
+  ===========================================
+    Header: FOUND
+    Test Case: 1
+    Expected Reason: 2
+    Actual Reason: 2
+    Report Sequence: 0
+  ===========================================
+  Reason code 2 = APP_ASSERT
+  VERIFICATION: PASSED (reason code matches)
+
+  ===========================================
+  Total reports: 1, Verified: 1
+  ===========================================
+
+
+CONFIGURATION
+-------------
+
+  CONFIG_CRASH_REPORT                               Required, kernel side
+  CONFIG_EXAMPLES_CRASHRPT_COMPREHENSIVE_TEST       This application
+  CONFIG_EXAMPLES_CRASHRPT_COMPREHENSIVE_TEST_DIR   Report directory (default: /mnt)
+  CONFIG_EXAMPLES_CRASHRPT_COMPREHENSIVE_TEST_PRIORITY  Reporter priority (default: 254)
+  CONFIG_EXAMPLES_CRASHRPT_COMPREHENSIVE_TEST_STACKSIZE  Reporter stack (default: 8192)
+
+
+NOTES
+-----
+
+1. The reporter priority MUST be higher than all other runnable threads.
+   If the priority is too low, the deadline may expire before the reporter
+   is scheduled and no report will be produced.
+
+2. The directory specified by CONFIG_EXAMPLES_CRASHRPT_COMPREHENSIVE_TEST_DIR
+   must be a writable mount point. On a real product, a raw partition or
+   append-only log is safer than a mounted filesystem.
+
+3. TC2 (KERNEL_ASSERT) triggers a kernel assert via ioctl on /dev/null.
+   The dev_null driver contains ASSERT((void *)arg == NULL) which triggers
+   when a non-NULL argument is passed to any ioctl command.
+
+4. Hardware faults and asserts raised from interrupt context cannot be
+   served by the reporter. Those cases need data published before the fault.
+
+
+TEST CASES SUMMARY
+------------------
+
++------+------------------+------------+---------------------------+
+|  TC  | Test Name        | Reason     | Description               |
++------+------------------+------------+---------------------------+
+|  1   | app_assert       | 2 (APP)    | Direct ASSERT(0) call     |
+|  2   | kernel_assert    | 3 (KERNEL) | ioctl on /dev/null with   |
+|      |                  |            | non-NULL arg triggers     |
+|      |                  |            | kernel ASSERT()           |
++------+------------------+------------+---------------------------+
+
+
+REASON CODES
+------------
+
+  1 = CRASHRPT_REASON_UNKNOWN     - No reporter or undetermined cause
+  2 = CRASHRPT_REASON_APP_ASSERT  - Application called ASSERT()
+  3 = CRASHRPT_REASON_KERNEL_ASSERT - Kernel called ASSERT()
+  4 = CRASHRPT_REASON_HW_FAULT    - Hardware fault or CPU exception

+apps/examples/crashrpt_test
+===========================
+
+Demonstration of the crash diagnostic capture driver, /dev/crashrpt.
+
+What it does
+------------
+
+The example holds a body of diagnostic data in memory and registers a
+reporter thread that serialises all of it to a file when the system is about
+to assert.
+
+  500 nodes of 48 bytes
+   50 nodes of 64 bytes
+  each node carries a message string of up to 255 bytes
+
+The message is not stored inside the node - the node holds a pointer to it.
+On disk the message follows its node, so both end up in the report.
+
+Sequence
+--------
+
+  1. The application builds the node data at start-up, while the system is
+     healthy.
+  2. The reporter thread registers through /dev/crashrpt and parks in
+     fin_wait().
+  3. An assert occurs.  At the very top of up_assert(), before any crash
+     handling begins, the kernel wakes the reporter and waits.
+  4. The reporter writes the report and tells the driver it is finished.
+  5. Assert handling continues and the board reboots.
+
+Why the data is built up front
+------------------------------
+
+Allocating several hundred blocks while the system is on its way down is
+exactly the kind of work that should not be attempted.  Building the data
+during normal operation also mirrors how a real product would accumulate
+diagnostic state.
+
+Temporary file and rename
+-------------------------
+
+The report is written to
+
+  <dir>/crashrpt.tmp
+
+and only after the write has completed and been flushed with fsync() is it
+renamed to
+
+  <dir>/crashrpt_r<n>.bin
+
+A reader therefore never observes a partially written report.  The final
+name either exists and is complete, or it does not exist at all.  If any
+step fails the temporary file is removed.
+
+File format
+-----------
+
+  Header, 32 bytes
+    magic     u32   0x54505243, "CRPT"
+    version   u32
+    reason    u32   the reason code passed by the kernel
+    n48       u32   number of 48 byte nodes
+    n64       u32   number of 64 byte nodes
+    sz48      u32   sizeof the 48 byte node
+    sz64      u32   sizeof the 64 byte node
+    reserved  u32
+
+  Then n48 records:
+    node      48 bytes, raw
+    msglen    u8
+    msg       msglen bytes, no terminator
+
+  Then n64 records:
+    node      64 bytes, raw
+    msglen    u8
+    msg       msglen bytes, no terminator
+
+The message pointer inside each node is zeroed in the copy that is written,
+since its value has no meaning outside the running process.  This also keeps
+the output reproducible.
+
+A one byte length field is sufficient because the message is capped at 255
+bytes.
+
+Largest possible report:
+
+  32 + 500 * (48 + 1 + 255) + 50 * (64 + 1 + 255) = 168032 bytes
+
+Actual size is smaller, as message lengths cycle through 32, 96, 160 and 255
+so that the boundary case is exercised regularly.
+
+Usage
+-----
+
+From TASH:
+
+  crashrpt_test init      Build the data and register the reporter
+  crashrpt_test status    Show current state and the largest possible report
+  crashrpt_test crash     Raise an assert to exercise the whole path
+
+A normal run looks like:
+
+  TASH>> crashrpt_test init
+  crashrpt_test: built 500 nodes of 48 bytes and 50 nodes of 64 bytes
+  crashrpt_test: reporter registered and waiting
+  crashrpt_test: ready, run 'crashrpt_test crash' to exercise it
+
+  TASH>> crashrpt_test crash
+  crashrpt_test: asserting now, the reporter should run before reboot
+  crashrpt_test: woken, reason 2
